request: RM7 tier 2: move unit conversion to write time. Rename the 15 unit-bearing vehicle_snapshots columns, convert the 6 value-changing ones in-place in the migration, convert in snapshotFrom via the tesla adapter's companions, delete the 6 read companions and both conversion constants, regenerate sqlc.

git.note: Shared RM7 branch. RD8: this tier leaves internal/battery and internal/gateway not compiling until tiers 3-4 land on this same branch.

tasks.notes: Design gate presented and confirmed by the user (decision D1). Index plan verified against the live catalog; pkey omission recorded as D2.
Created migration file byte-identical to design.md D1's SQL block (diffed, zero delta).
Verified: Up renames all 15 columns; UPDATE rescales exactly the 6 value-changing ones (battery_range_km, odometer_km, 4 tpms_*_psi); the 9 rename-only columns are absent from the SET list.
Verified: Down divides the 6 rescaled columns then renames all 15 back in reverse order; no column or row dropped anywhere.

Round-trip on a disposable container: 12000mi->19312.128km, 2.9bar->42.060944psi, NULL stayed NULL, temps unchanged. Down restored 12000 / 210.50000000000003 / 2.9 - float tolerance exactly as design D1 predicted.
query.sql InsertVehicleSnapshot column list, VALUES param names, and ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET block renamed for all 15 affected columns.
ListSnapshotsByVehicle, SnapshotsByVehicleSince, and LatestSnapshotsByAccount column lists renamed to match.
Rewrote InsertVehicleSnapshot header comment (removed the miles/derived-on-read claim) and the TPMS bar comment to state PSI conversion happens once at capture time via the tesla adapter companions.
Ran `sqlc generate`; db/query.sql.go and models.go regenerated with renamed struct fields (OdometerKm, BatteryRangeKm, TpmsPressureFlPsi, etc) verified via grep.

Snapshot fields renamed with unit suffix (BatteryRangeKm, OdometerKm, InsideTempC, OutsideTempC, BatteryLevelPct, UsableBatteryLevelPct, ChargeLimitSocPct, ChargeEnergyAddedKWh, ChargerPowerKW, ChargerVoltageV, ChargerActualCurrentA, TpmsPressure{FL,FR,RL,RR}PSI); unit comments updated.
Deleted the 6 companion methods (BatteryRangeKm, OdometerKm, 4x TpmsPressure*PSI) — required for the field renames to compile (design D4).
Deleted milesToKm and barToPSI constants from telemetry.go; module now has zero conversion factors (verified via grep).

mapping.go rowToSnapshot updated for both renamed generated-struct fields (r.OdometerKm, r.TpmsPressureFlPsi, etc.) and renamed domain Snapshot fields.
Verified Reader interface (LatestSnapshotsByAccount, SnapshotsByVehicleSince) method signatures are unchanged — only Snapshot field names changed.
Grepped internal/telemetry non-test source for calls to the 6 deleted companions and old field names — none found; reader.go/scheduler.go/wake.go were already clean.

Renamed Snapshot fields across db_integration_test.go, db_read_integration_test.go, db_sourcea_integration_test.go, reader_test.go, service_test.go. Restated BatteryRange/Odometer literals as their km equivalents (x1.609344, e.g. 210.5mi->338.766912km) so no test silently kept a miles value under a km field name; %, kWh, kW, V, A fields were already display-native so only field names changed, no values.

Added TestSnapshotFrom_ConvertsToDisplayUnits in new snapshot_from_test.go: known miles/bar tesla.VehicleDataTesla -> literal expected km/PSI on Snapshot (80.4672, 19312.128, 42.0609439417 etc, mirroring internal/tesla's TestMetricCompanions/TestTpmsPressurePSICompanions house style, not milesToKm/barToPSI since those no longer exist here).

Documented this in TestSnapshotFrom_TPMS_UnreportedVsZero; the true nil case (pre-migration DB row) is proven end-to-end by TestTPMS_NilRoundTrip in db_tpms_integration_test.go (task 5.4).

All DATABASE_URL-gated tests pass against a testcontainers-provisioned Postgres.

Did NOT edit ai/go-conventions.md or root CLAUDE.md (owned by platform-unit-of-measure-convention). Full tree fails ONLY in internal/battery (derive.go: UsableBatteryLevel, BatteryLevel, OdometerKm()) and internal/gateway/handlers (handlers.go: BatteryLevel, BatteryRangeKm(), OdometerKm(), InsideTemp, OutsideTemp). Both truncated by "too many errors" - tiers 3/4 will find more in history.go.

decisions.decision: DATABASE DESIGN GATE CONFIRMED. The user approved the migration exactly as specified in design.md D1/D2: 15 RENAME COLUMN statements, one UPDATE rescaling the 6 value-changing columns (x1.609344 / x14.503773773), types, nullability, constraints and indexes untouched.
decisions.why: Leader presented the full DDL, the backfill semantics (NULL*factor=NULL preserves the not-reported invariant; a truthful 0.0 stays non-NULL; updated_at deliberately not bumped), the rollback story, the rejected alternatives, and an index plan VERIFIED against the live catalog rather than the design doc. User answered 'Confirmed - apply as designed'.

decisions.decision: design.md D2 says vehicle_snapshots has 'exactly two indexed objects'; the live catalog has THREE (vehicle_snapshots_pkey on (id) is omitted from the doc). Left uncorrected at the user's choice; recorded here instead.
decisions.why: Surfaced to the user at the gate. The conclusion is unaffected - `id` is not among the 15 renamed columns, so no index still references a renamed column - and the user chose 'apply as designed' over 'fix the doc first'. Recorded so the reviewer does not read the prose/reality mismatch as a design deviation.

decisions.decision: The migration must NOT be applied to the real database (localhost:5432/magus) during tiers 2-3. The user runs `make migrate-up` themselves after tier 4.
decisions.why: User chose 'Not until tier 4 is done'. Applying tier 2 alone would leave the schema ahead of any still-running old poller binary, which would write miles into a column named odometer_km. Implementation and tests need only disposable testcontainers, so nothing is lost by waiting.

decisions.decision: Tasks 1.5, 1.6 and all of group 7 are leader-run, not worker-run; workers are forbidden from make migrate-up/migrate-down entirely.
decisions.why: Those targets read DATABASE_URL from .env, which points at the user's real database - and D3 puts it off limits. The leader performs the migrate round-trip on a disposable container instead. Group 7 also reaches outside the module sandbox (7.4 deliberately builds the whole tree to capture the expected battery/gateway failures for tiers 3-4).

decisions.decision: Accepted the worker's deletion of internal/telemetry/tpms_test.go after independently verifying no coverage was lost.
decisions.why: That file tested the domain-level Snapshot.TpmsPressure*PSI() companions on *float64 fields - both deleted by design D4, so its subject no longer exists. Its two behaviours are re-covered: NULL round-trip by TestTPMS_NilRoundTrip (asserts Valid=false at the DB layer) and conversion correctness by internal/tesla's TestTpmsPressurePSICompanions plus the new TestSnapshotFrom_ConvertsToDisplayUnits. A deleted test is normally an anti-gaming red flag; this one was checked, not trusted.

decisions.decision: Task 5.3's literal wording ('an unreported TPMS reading stays nil through snapshotFrom') is UNSATISFIABLE, and so is the matching clause of roadmap RD12. Accepted the worker's honest partial implementation rather than a false assertion.
decisions.why: tesla.VehicleStateTesla's four TPMS fields are plain float64, so encoding/json collapses 'key absent' and 'reported 0.0' into the same zero value and ptr() ALWAYS yields non-nil. Verified this predates RM7: the pre-change service.go did ptr(data.VehicleState.TpmsPressureFL) on the same plain float64. NULL therefore only ever means 'pre-migration row', never 'not reported'. RD12's claim that snapshotFrom creates the nil distinction is wrong as written. Not fixed here - it is a roadmap/spec wording defect, not a code defect, and belongs to whoever next touches that spec.
